messages.text: How do changes in AI data centers technology affect the measurement capability required from Signal Generator / Signal Analyzer?

I couldn’t retrieve grounded evidence from the installed RS knowledge source for this specific question, so the points below are a general engineering assessment.

AI data centers are pushing measurement needs in Signal Generators and Signal/Spectrum Analyzers in several directions:

| Technology change in AI data centers | Impact on required signal generation / analysis capability |
|---|---|
| Faster interconnects: 400G/800G/1.6T Ethernet, PCIe Gen5/6/7, CXL, high-speed SerDes | Instruments need much wider modulation / analysis bandwidth, high sample-rate capture, excellent timing accuracy, and support for complex eye/EVM/jitter-type characterization. |
| More advanced modulation and signaling: PAM4, future PAM6/PAM8-like schemes, coherent optics | Signal generators must create precise stressed waveforms with controlled noise, jitter, skew and channel loss. Analyzers need accurate EVM, BER-related diagnostics, equalization support, and impairment decomposition. |
| Higher clock rates and tighter timing margins | Phase noise and jitter performance become more critical. Generators need ultra-low-jitter clocks and analyzers need very low residual jitter / phase-noise measurement floors. |
| Dense GPU/accelerator boards and high-current power delivery | Power integrity and EMI issues increase. Spectrum/signal analyzers need better sensitivity, wide dynamic range, near-field/EMI debug capability, and time-correlated spectral analysis. |
| Co-packaged optics / optical-electrical convergence | Test setups increasingly need synchronized electrical and optical measurement paths, high bandwidth, precise trigger alignment, and support for transceiver stress and compliance testing. |
| Liquid cooling, dense rack integration, and high power switching | More switching noise, conducted/radiated emissions, and transient events. Real-time spectrum analysis and long-duration capture become more valuable. |
| More AI workload burstiness | Measurement must capture intermittent, non-stationary behavior, not just steady-state signals. Analyzers benefit from real-time bandwidth, spectrograms, trigger-on-event, and deep memory. |
| Faster product cycles and large-scale validation | Automation, remote control, repeatable test scripts, high-throughput measurements, and multi-channel/multi-site testing become more important. |

In short: AI data centers move the requirement from “measure a clean, stable signal” toward “generate and analyze very wideband, high-speed, impaired, time-varying signals with tight jitter, phase-noise, EVM, EMI, and automation requirements.”

For Signal Generators, the key capability shift is toward:

- higher output bandwidth,
- cleaner clocks and lower phase noise,
- arbitrary waveform generation for stressed signals,
- calibrated impairment injection,
- multi-channel synchronization,
- support for high-speed digital / optical interface test scenarios.

For Signal Analyzers, the key shift is toward:

- wider analysis bandwidth,
- lower noise floor and wider dynamic range,
- real-time spectrum capture,
- better phase noise / jitter / modulation quality analysis,
- time-correlated frequency-domain diagnostics,
- EMI / EMC debug capability,
- automated compliance and production test support.
